citation.title: Deep learning for plasma tomography using the bolometer system at JET
citation.authors: F.A. Matos, D.R. Ferreira, P.J. Carvalho, JET Contributors

topic: Up-convolutional neural network that maps JET KB5 bolometer readings to 2D radiated-emission tomograms
own_question: Can a deep network reproduce existing regularization-based tomograms pixel by pixel from 1D projection data?
actual_method_and_evidence: The input is PCA-reduced KB5 channels (50 components) at a single time slice. The output is a 120×200 image. Training used existing tomograms as labels, with about 18k reconstructions from ILW campaigns. Data were split randomly 80/10/10 within each campaign group. The paper reports mean SSIM of 0.97–0.99 and mean NRMSE of about 0.02–0.04 on the test sets. Results are offline only. No timing of inference was reported.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Same-time-slice mapping from bolometer data to tomogram. It involves no temporal nowcasting, no past-report inputs, and no CES or ion temperature.
validation_if_relevant: Random within-campaign split. Temporal or pulse independence is unknown. No untouched campaign was held out.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim it shows real-time capability; real-time use is only envisioned.
Do not equate radiated-power tomography with impurity Ti or with CES nowcasting.
Do not cite it as evidence that prior work is noncausal.
Do not treat the tomogram labels as physical truth; the authors note that artifacts in the labels are reproduced by the network.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: The source is only loosely related. At most it could support a brief mention that neural surrogates have been trained to reproduce conventional diagnostic reconstruction outputs. It has no bearing on causal nowcasting of CES temperature or on BES/ECEI inputs. Optional; likely exclude.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
